pr_title: Add granular error list to alias action response
pr_comment: Hi @parkertimmins, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
I will take a look on Monday, if you're willing to wait until then, @parkertimmins.

review_comment: I think we're missing an `IndicesAliasesResponseTests` class that extends `AbstractWireSerializingTestCase` to ensure we test the `StreamInput/Output` serialization.

It's out of scope for this PR, but I really think we ought to refactor this method in another PR. For a block of code that does something so simple, It is incredibly confusing to keep track of what is going on in here.

I am a little uncomfortable with the change made in this file. Specifically, the use of the actionResult variable which is modified throughout the main loop over actions. Also, the fact the the action result is added to the final actionResults list at different places in the code. This is done because of the use of `continue`  in a few places. I think a better design would require a refactor of this loop to remove the use of `continue` statements. I was trying to avoid changing the code too much ... but kinda seems like I already passed that point.
We can leave the refactor as a follow-up, if you want to open an issue for it. I agree that it'd be nicer to write it in more of a functional style.

@dakrone 
I found that rest yaml tests failed due to the differences in resolved index names when using security and unresolved names without security.

 So I added this logic with `resolvedIndices` to use the actual indices when security is not enabled. This [commit](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/106514/commits/e3d5ce57334223301c66969225a4c45f5ed61f3f) specifically.

If you think this is too messy, I'd suggest we remove action information entirely from the action result, leaving only status code and optional error info. The error will still contain the missing alias name which will probably be enough info to diagnose the issue.The action information could be added back in the follow-up once this class is a bit clearer.
I think this is reasonable, thanks
